headline_marked: Historic rise: [[Bangladesh climb to record sixth]] in ICC Test rankings
headline: Historic rise: Bangladesh climb to record sixth in ICC Test rankings
summary: The Tigers reach a new peak in Test cricket despite a series-ending loss to Australia, moving ahead of Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
details: Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings. The team now holds 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.
This achievement marks a new high for the Tigers, surpassing their previous best ranking of seventh achieved in May this year after a home series win against Pakistan.

The rise follows a 1-1 draw during their tour of Australia, highlighted by a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin. However, the tour ended with a defeat in Mackay, where Australia won by an innings and 51 runs.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described the climb to number six as a 'massive achievement,' though he noted the team's performance in the final Test was not ideal.
With this jump, Bangladesh has moved ahead of several teams, including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, West Indies, and Zimbabwe.
In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a percentage of 55.56, narrowly staying ahead of India.
The Tigers have played six WTC matches in the current cycle, recording three wins, two losses, and one draw. Their next challenge will be a two-Test series in South Africa.
caption:
A historic first for the Tigers! 🇧🇩 Bangladesh has officially climbed to a record sixth in the ICC Test rankings.

Bangladesh has climbed three places to reach a record sixth position in the ICC Test rankings. The team now holds 78 rating points, placing them behind Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, India, and England.

This achievement marks a new high for the Tigers, surpassing their previous best ranking of seventh achieved in May this year after a home series win against Pakistan.

The rise follows a 1-1 draw during their tour of Australia, highlighted by a historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin. However, the tour ended with a defeat in Mackay, where Australia won by an innings and 51 runs.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto described the climb to number six as a 'massive achievement,' though he noted the team's performance in the final Test was not ideal.

With this jump, Bangladesh has moved ahead of several teams, including Sri Lanka, Pakistan, West Indies, and Zimbabwe.

In the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 table, Bangladesh remains in fourth place with 40 points and a percentage of 55.56, narrowly staying ahead of India.

The Tigers have played six WTC matches in the current cycle, recording three wins, two losses, and one draw. Their next challenge will be a two-Test series in South Africa.
